title: People Are Creating ‘Survival Guides’ to Cope With the ‘AO3 Apocalypse’
gist: Archive of Our Own, with 11 million users and over 18 million works, went down on October 29 for a 'security incident' that may take up to four weeks to resolve, prompting fans to circulate offline 'survival guides'.

insights.claim: AO3 went down on October 29 for a security incident and warned restoration could take up to four weeks, though a degraded state may return sooner; it does not believe its user database was stolen but urged password changes.
insights.speaker: Ej Dickson
insights.so_what: Large UGC platforms run by nonprofits face resilience and security-funding risk.
insights.locator: On October 29, an admin for AO3 posted

insights.claim: AO3 hosts more than 18 million works and has 11 million users, with a surge of tens of thousands of stories after the Heated Rivalry TV series.
insights.speaker: Ej Dickson
insights.so_what: Scale shows how concentrated fan creation is on a single platform.

insights.claim: Fan fiction drives mainstream publishing trends and the vertical video industry, with streaming platforms scouring fan fiction sites for adaptable works.
insights.speaker: Ej Dickson
insights.so_what: Fan-fiction platforms are an IP pipeline for media companies.

insights.claim: Fans are compiling Google Docs of downloaded stories as 'survival guides', one of which struggles with heavy traffic.
insights.speaker: Ej Dickson
insights.so_what: Outages push users to unofficial copies, raising copyright and moderation issues.
insights.locator: Other fans are compiling Google Docs
